content: 1. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, which can result in increased activity of CYP enzymes. It is essential to monitor for reduced systemic levels of narrow therapeutic or sensitive CYP substrates that are influenced by CYP inducers after initiating nemolizumab. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. 2. Oral neomycin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 4. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of nicardipine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 5. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Nirmatrelvir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be considered for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is possibly related to ritonavir-induced CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 7. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods should be used for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is possibly related to ritonavir-induced CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction. 8. Nitrofurantoin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Ethinyl estradiol may decrease the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially increasing serum concentrations of antidepressants and the risk of TCA-related adverse effects. Close monitoring is recommended. 10. Ofloxacin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of olanzapine by affecting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 13. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir with or without dasabuvir is contraindicated with ethinyl estradiol due to the risk of significant ALT elevations observed in clinical trials. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating this hepatitis C combination regimen and restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 14. Otesecozole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and toxicity risks of BCRP substrates, including ethinyl estradiol. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Consider reducing the dose of BCRP substrates. 15. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 16. Paromomycin reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Penicillin G aqueous decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by increasing its metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended due to the risk of oral contraceptive failure. 18. Penicillin VK reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 20. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 21. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 22. Pioglitazone decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 24. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 25. Ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 26. Oral contraceptives inhibit the N-demethylation of selegiline, potentially increasing its levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 27. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated by infection and inflammation stimuli. Caution is advised when coadministering with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 28. Oral estrogens may reduce serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs, potentially requiring higher GH doses. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 29. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Alternative drugs or nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 30. Sugammadex may bind to progestogen, reducing its exposure and potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Patients should use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for seven days after sugammadex administration. 31. Sulfadiazine reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Sulfamethoxazole reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Sulfisoxazole reduces the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 35. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary.
